output.name: Ommen

anatomy.part: lantern hung from the bow on its rope

output.myth: When the sea took my cousin's boat off the Leeward rocks, we did what we always do. At the harbour mouth we said every name aloud, and for each name we lit a lantern and set it on Ommen's rail. Ommen is a boat built of salt-wood and promises. She sails up into Vel with her lamps, and the drowned sit in her hold mending their nets. Kael the Netter casts from her stern for the fallen stars and has never hauled one in, which is why he is so cheerful. Sil, the Drowned Lantern, sees the boat from her high window and comes down each month to count the lamps, because she is still looking for Aun, and some nights she thinks he is in the hold. Orrun shifts beneath the hull and the sea goes quiet. Hesk will not say when the boat will come home. So keep saying the names. A lamp is light enough for anyone to carry.
output.verse:
Halun on the bow,
each name said, one lamp for each—
Ommen carries them.
